versions.change: Original Wishbone interconnect concept by Wade D. Peterson of Silicore Corporation. Defined the basic point-to-point and shared-bus topologies, SINGLE / BLOCK / RMW cycle types, and standard MASTER / SLAVE signal set.
Released 2002 (referenced as the predecessor to B.4). Introduced the [LOCK_O] / [LOCK_I] signals and additional tag-type definitions.

Released 2010 by OpenCores under stewardship of Richard Herveille. Added Chapter 4 — WISHBONE Registered Feedback Bus Cycles ([CTI_O()] / [CTI_I()] Cycle Type Identifier and [BTE_O()] / [BTE_I()] Burst Type Extension tags) on top of the existing Classic bus cycles. Also added explicit pipelined-mode rules (Section 3.1.3.2) using [STALL_I] / [STALL_O]. Detailed revision history maintained at www.silicore.net/wishbone.htm.

deprecated_features.deprecated_in_version: Not deprecated in B.4 (Wishbone B4 still uses MASTER / SLAVE terminology, in contrast to AMBA AHB Issue C which moved to Manager / Subordinate).
deprecated_features.rationale: Backwards compatibility — Wishbone has used MASTER / SLAVE since the original spec; the B4 spec preserves these names.

backward_compat_traps.issue_B4: Adds Registered Feedback as an OPTIONAL extension. Rule 4.00 — every Registered Feedback compatible core MUST also support Classic cycles. Rule 4.10 — if either side doesn't implement a burst type, the cycle MUST complete as a Classic [CTI_IO()=3'b000] cycle. Backward compatible by design.

backward_compat_traps.issue_B3: Pipelined handshake not formally defined (existed only as a customization).
backward_compat_traps.issue_B4: Section 3.1.3.2 codifies pipelined mode using the [STALL_I] / [STALL_O] signal. Cores must declare in the DATASHEET whether they support standard, pipelined, or both.

backward_compat_traps.rule: If a MASTER does not implement [ERR_I] / [RTY_I] / [LOCK_O] / [CTI_O()] / [BTE_O()] / [STALL_I], the optional signal MUST be tied to its inactive default (0 / 3'b000 / 2'b00) at the integration boundary.
User-defined tags ([TGA] / [TGD] / [TGC]) are NOT semantically interchangeable between cores — each core defines its own tag meanings in its DATASHEET (RULE 3.70 + RULE 2.15 item 6).
Standard mode allows asynchronous SLAVE [ACK_O] (combinational from [STB_I]+[CYC_I]); higher-speed designs SHOULD use registered [ACK_O] (OBSERVATION 3.50) at the cost of one wait state per transfer.
RULE 2.30: All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active HIGH logic. Active-LOW interface signals are NOT permitted. Active-LOW system reset must be inverted before driving [RST_I].
A BLOCK cycle keeps [CYC_O] asserted across phases. To hold ownership of a shared SLAVE across multiple BLOCK phases through an arbiter, the MASTER MUST also assert [LOCK_O].

fields.version_naming_history_note: Wishbone revisions before B.3 are summarized at www.silicore.net/wishbone.htm. The B.3 -> B.4 transition is the most significant — it added Chapter 4 Registered Feedback bus cycles AND formalized the pipelined-mode handshake. Both Classic (Chapter 3) and Registered Feedback (Chapter 4) cycles are part of B.4; Classic remains mandatory for all B.4 cores.
interoperability_summary: A B.4 MASTER that implements Registered Feedback can drive a B.3 SLAVE by issuing only Classic cycles (CTI_O=3'b000) — RULE 4.00 / RULE 4.10 guarantee backwards compatibility.
A B.4 SLAVE that implements only Classic MUST treat any [CTI_I()] inputs from a Registered Feedback MASTER as if [CTI_I()]=3'b000 (RULE 4.10).

A pipelined MASTER and a standard SLAVE can interoperate if the master implements [STALL_I] handling (Section 5.2.1 — 'Using [STALL_I] to avoid pipelining' — STALL_I asserted to disable pipelining behavior).
A standard MASTER and a pipelined SLAVE can interoperate via a wrapper (Section 5.1 — a finite-state machine bridges [STB_O] / [ACK_I] timing).
Off-chip Wishbone interfaces operate at lower speeds than on-chip but use the identical protocol (Section 1.2 / Figure 1-6).

evidence.quote: The various revisions of the WISHBONE specification, along with their changes and revision history, can be found at www.silicore.net/wishbone.htm.

evidence.spec_section: Chapter 4 WISHBONE Registered Feedback Bus Cycles
evidence.quote: To achieve the highest possible throughput, WISHBONE Classic requires asynchronous cycle termination signals. ... In large System-on-Chip devices this routing delay between MASTER and SLAVE is the dominant timing factor. ... The simplest solution for reducing the delay is to cut the loop, by using synchronous cycle termination signals. However, this introduces a wait state for every transfer.

All WISHBONE Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST support WISHBONE Classic bus cycles. MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that do support the [CTI_I()] and [CTI_O()] signals MUST at least support the Classic cycle [CTI_IO()='000'] and the End-of-Cycle [CTI_IO()='111'].
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that are designed to support a limited number of burst types MUST complete the unsupported cycles as though they were WISHBONE Classic cycle, i.e. [CTI_IO()='000'].
All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active high logic.
The lock output [LOCK_O] when asserted, indicates that the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. (Introduced in Wishbone B.3.)

evidence.spec_section: Chapter 5 Interfacing standard and pipelined peripherals
evidence.quote: Section 5.1 — Standard master connected to pipelined slave. Section 5.2.1 — Using [STALL_I] to avoid pipelining: a master with [STALL_I] asserted will not initiate new transactions until the [STALL_I] condition is negated.
